title: M1-01: Contracts v1.2: reconcile every doc's names into contracts.md (blocks every task)
body:
## Goal

Land contracts v1.2 (the v1.1 reconcile plus the 2026-10-11 decisions) as the first PR, before anything else merges: after it, contracts.md is the only list of shared names. The PR folds every 'New names' section of the four layout docs, the four flow docs and plan section 11 into contracts §15 and removes those sections; gives each row of plan section 10 its answer (contracts §16), including the contradictions this wave found (votes, managed vLLM, the settings table, catalog collisions; rows 38–44); settles the catalog collisions (contracts §10.2) so M1-13 only writes files; and puts every doc that lost a conflict in line with a one-line pointer. It carries the owner decisions of 2026-10-10 that aren't frontend: ADR-0034 accepted (one-time login codes for an HttpOnly session cookie, the shell only runs `rastai open --print-url`, the loopback Host rule, a too-open `owner.token` refuses the start, `Register` before `Hello` on reattach), with the status lines of ADR-0001, ADR-0006 and ADR-0007; ADR-0033 and ADR-0037 cited by contracts §2.5 and §12.5; one owner per algorithm (contracts §2.4 rule 10); the user-namespace fallback (contracts §8.8); the (L2) tags; and the long-term archive names (0.5 day, ADR-0035): crate `rastai-archive`, the `archive.*` commands and events, settings section `archive`, keychain accounts `archive.mysql` and `archive.objects`, `source_id`, `archive_cursors`, `runs.archive_state`, the `vault_changes` outbox, the archive tables of contracts §8.7, `MysqlConnection` and the range `RRS-S5xxx`. The ADR index's 'Notes since acceptance' table records every language and path fix. With the owner decisions of 2026-10-11 it lands contracts v1.2 and ADR-0038: §15 accepted, not provisional, and a milestone mark such as "(M4)" on every registered name that isn't built yet, so `check-names` passes the day M1-57 lands.

## Files and modules

- `docs/architecture/contracts.md` (v1.2, with its 'Changes in v1.1' and v1.2 lists)
- `docs/adr/0038-naming-and-schema-enforcement.md`

- `docs/architecture/flows/*.md` (the same)
- `docs/adr/0034-login-codes-loopback-host-owner-token.md`, `docs/adr/0035-mysql-long-term-archive.md` and `docs/adr/0037-borrowed-decoders-and-parser-fuzzing.md`
- the status lines of `docs/adr/0001-process-layout.md`, `0002-durability-worker-event-logs.md`, `0003-storage-sqlite-vault-blobs.md`, `0006-ui-transport-http-only.md`, `0007-local-api-security.md` and `0029-strict-safetensors-contract.md`

- `docs/architecture/README.md`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` (sections 10 and 11) and `docs/plan/backlog.json`

## Acceptance test

Docs-only PR, exempt from the test rule (plan 3.3). Review checklist in the PR: no layout or flow doc keeps a 'New names' section, and every name they use is in contracts.md or in contracts §15.11 as rejected with its replacement; every row of plan section 10 has one answer in contracts §16; the archive names of ADR-0035 are all in contracts; every superseded ADR decision points to the ADR that replaced it; no doc names a `settings` table, a managed vLLM engine in the prototype or `votes.jsonl`; every registered name that isn't built yet carries its milestone mark, "(M1)" included.

## Depends on

none

## Lane and size

Lane A (mostly contracts, the control plane and the UI); size L + 0.5 (about 2.5 days; two PRs under this issue).

## Done when

Docs-only PR: the test rule doesn't apply (plan §3.3). The review checklist in the acceptance test replaces it.

**Closed only after independent verification** (plan §3.6): `just check` passes locally (the pre-push hook enforces it), including `check-names` and `check-schema-diff` once M1-57 and M1-58 have landed; a reviewer agent that is not the author runs `just check` on a fresh clone of the exact PR head and confirms each acceptance criterion above against the code and the command output; that evidence is posted as the closing comment. title: M1-26: rastai-server: startup, listeners, request gate and origin-bound sign-in
body:
## Goal

`run_daemon` as the thin sequence of platform flow 2.1 (the embedded node call is a stub until M1-47), the Server struct, clean shutdown, owner.token and identity keys, the loopback TCP listener on 47820–47829 and daemon.sock with TCP_NODELAY, the request gate (Host, Origin, credentials; any loopback Host on any port, ADR-0034), one-time login codes and session cookies, the Connect envelopes and the hand-written Connect JSON for the CommandService messages, and `/api/health` with `apis`, `plugin_api` and `node_protocol`. **Sessions are bound to the origin that redeemed the login code** (owner decision N4): browsers send a loopback cookie to every port, so `POST /api/login` must carry Origin, the session stores it as `bound_origin`, and a cookie request from any other origin is refused. title: M1-34: Safetensors: the one header check in rastai-formats, and the Python reader and writer that call it (spike port)
body:

## Goal

title: M8-E02: Install pipeline and trust
body:
## Goal

Local install of a .rrsplugin with a trust prompt, and 'install missing' for files that need plugins.

## Scope

Cut into PR-sized tasks (half a day to two days each) when the milestone starts.

- plugin.install plan and apply (hashes, permissions, plugin lockfile layered on the base environment), uninstall, enable, disable
- plugin.suggest, the missing-plugins banner and placeholder nodes; permission enforcement
- **Reserve first-party plugin ids.** A manifest whose `plugin_id` is a first-party id (the `FIRST_PARTY_CAPABILITIES` plugin ids, today `psychology` and `eval`, `crates/rastai-server/src/plugin_host/capabilities.rs` `is_first_party_plugin_id`) and that is not the preinstalled copy with the release's content hash is refused with `RRS-P0002`, at install and at discovery. Today first-party status is decided by id alone (`load.rs`), and those ids aren't in `rastai-formats`' reserved `CORE_AREAS`, so a dev-path or installed plugin with that id would provide first-party capabilities. (`check_module_isolation` already requires preinstalled plus the release hash, so the namespace exemption itself is safe.)
- **Cap the manifest.** Read `rastai-plugin.json` with a bounded read (for example 1 MiB, a constant beside `MANIFEST_FILE_NAME`) instead of the unbounded `std::fs::read` in `plugin_host/discovery.rs` `read_manifest`, and pass `ImportLimits` with that `max_file_bytes` (the default allows 64 MiB). A larger manifest is `failed` with `RRS-P0001`; install refuses it before the trust prompt.
- **Re-check on `plugin.enable`.** Enabling a plugin runs negotiation for it and then re-checks every `disabled`/`incompatible` plugin whose diagnostic is `RRS-P1002` or `RRS-P3001` naming it, in load order until nothing changes. This is the reverse of `disable_plugin`'s cascade (`load.rs`), so a dependency chain comes back with its first link instead of at the next start.
- the plugin-data downgrade guard (`RRS-P3005`) is (L2), in M10-E04

## Exit test

An archive changed after the prompt is refused (RRS-P2003); an interrupted install leaves nothing (kill -9 row 8); a file needing a missing plugin opens with placeholders; a dev or installed fixture with id `psychology` is refused with `RRS-P0002` and provides no first-party capability; a 2 MiB manifest is `failed` with `RRS-P0001` without being read whole; after disabling then enabling the Psychology plugin, a lens fixture that depends on it ends `enabled` again without a restart; a threat-model B10 row (A6, the manifest) points at these tests, with owner M8-E02.

body:
## Goal

## Scope

- `deny.toml`: `mysql_async` (feature `default-rustls-ring`) pinned to `rastai-archive`, imported only in `src/mysql.rs`
- **Owner decision first** (threat-model open question 7, R13): should one daemon's archive user be kept from reading other sources' rows? Default: no (every source is readable, and a lost machine's user is revoked at once). A yes means a database or views per source, which changes `tables.rs`, so it is settled before this epic's schema contract PR and recorded in ADR-0035 or the threat model; M11-E02 checks it is recorded
- `ArchiveConfigureArgs` (contracts 6.5) drops `password`, `object_access_key` and `object_secret_key`: the MySQL password is stored first with `secret.set` in the keychain account `archive.mysql` and named by `connection.password_secret` (`MysqlConnection`), and S3 keys go into `archive.objects` the same way.
